about.title: Lines: y = mx and y = mx + b
about.length_note: 35 minutes fits. There are four topics: y = mx, the starting value b, graphing, and writing from a graph. Each gets one example and one check question. Nothing was cut or stretched.

sources.title: 4.5 Use the Slope-Intercept Form of an Equation of a Line, Elementary Algebra 2e
Deriving the Equation y = mx+b
sources.publisher: CK-12 Foundation (Interactive Middle School Math 8 for CCSS)

sources.title: Graph Equations using Slope and Intercept

say.text: Welcome to class 11. Today a whole line becomes one short equation you can read like a label.

show.text: Lines: y = mx and y = mx + b

say.text: Four steps today, one at a time, with a check after each. Take your time. You can pause anywhere.

show.text:
1. Lines through the origin: y = mx
2. The y-intercept: a starting value
3. Graphing from slope and intercept
4. Writing an equation from a graph

say.text: First, a reminder from last class. Slope is rise over run: how far up for each step to the right.
Step one. If a line passes through the origin, the point (0, 0), its equation is y = mx. The letter m is the slope.
Try y = 2x. When x is 0, y is 0, so the line starts at the origin. Each step right adds 2 up.
Your turn. In y = 3x, what is y when x is 4?

ask.q: For the line y = 3x, what is y when x = 4?
ask.why: y = mx means y is m times x. Here that is 3 × 4 = 12. Adding gives 7. Writing the digits side by side gives 34. Dividing gives 1.33.

say.text: The slope can be a fraction too. A slope of one half means up 1 for every 2 steps right.

ask.q: A line goes through the origin and has slope 1/2. Which equation is it?
ask.why: A line through the origin is y = mx, and m is the slope, so m = 1/2. y = 2x is steeper, with slope 2. y = x + 1/2 has slope 1 and does not go through the origin. y = 1/2 is a flat line.

say.text: Why can we pick any two points to find the slope? On a straight line, the slope is the same between any two points.
The reason comes from similar triangles. You will meet those properly in class 26. For now, trust that the slope is the same everywhere on a line.
Step two. Not every line goes through the origin. The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis, at the point (0, b).
Think of b as a starting value. You begin with 1 dollar. Then you add 2 dollars each week. After x weeks, y = 2x + 1.
Here is that line. At x = 0 it starts at 1, not 0. After that it still climbs 2 for every 1 step right.
Compare the two lines. They have the same slope. Every y on the second line is 1 more, so it is the first line slid up by 1.

ask.q: How does the line y = 2x + 1 compare with the line y = 2x?
ask.right: It is the same line moved up 1.
wrong: It is the same line moved right 1.
It is the same line moved down 1.
ask.why: Every y-value on y = 2x + 1 is exactly 1 more than on y = 2x. That means the line is slid up by 1. The slope stays 2, so it is not steeper.

say.text: Now reading an equation. In y = mx + b, m is the number multiplying x, and b is the number added. Watch the signs.

show.text: m = the number with x (slope) | b = the number added on its own (y-intercept)

ask.q: In y = -3x + 8, what are m and b?
ask.why: The number with x is -3, so m = -3. The number added on its own is +8, so b = 8. Mixing up m and b is a common mistake. Keep the signs too, because the -3 is negative and the 8 is positive.

say.text: Step three, graphing. Plot the y-intercept first. Then use the slope to find a second point. Then draw the line.

show.text:
1. Plot (0, b)
2. From there, go up the rise and right the run
3. Draw a line through the points

say.text: Example: y = (2/3)x + 1. Start at (0, 1). The slope 2/3 means up 2, right 3. That lands on (3, 3). Do it again for (6, 5). Then draw the line.

show.text: A coordinate grid. Points at (0, 1), (3, 3) and (6, 5), with a straight line through them going up to the right.

ask.q: You want to graph y = 3x - 2. Which point do you plot first?
ask.why: The first point is always the y-intercept (0, b). Here b = -2, so it is (0, -2). The slope 3 is used afterwards, to move up 3 and right 1.

say.text: A negative slope means the line goes down as you move right. Take y = -(1/2)x + 3. Start at (0, 3). Go down 1 and right 2.

show.text: A coordinate grid. A point at (0, 3) and another at (2, 2), with a line sloping gently downward to the right.

ask.q: For y = -(1/2)x + 3, starting at (0, 3), which point is next?
ask.why: The slope -1/2 means down 1 for every 2 steps right. From (0, 3) that is right 2 and down 1, which lands on (2, 2). (2, 4) goes up, which would be a positive slope.

say.text: Step four, the reverse. Given a graph, find b where the line crosses the y-axis. Then find m from rise over run. Then put both into y = mx + b.

show.text:
1. Read b at the y-axis
2. Find m = rise ÷ run
3. Write y = mx + b

say.text: Example: a line crosses the y-axis at (0, -1) and also passes through (2, 2). From (0, -1) to (2, 2), the rise is 3 and the run is 2. So m = 3/2 and y = (3/2)x - 1.

show.text: A coordinate grid. A line crosses the y-axis at -1 and passes through (2, 2).

say.text: Always check with a point. Put x = 2 into y = (3/2)x - 1. You get 3 - 1 = 2. That matches the point (2, 2). Now you try one.

ask.q: A line crosses the y-axis at (0, 4) and passes through (2, 0). What is its equation?
ask.why: b = 4 because the line crosses the y-axis at 4. From (0, 4) to (2, 0) the line goes down 4 over a run of 2, so m = -4/2 = -2. That gives y = -2x + 4. Check: x = 2 gives -4 + 4 = 0, which matches. A positive 2 would mean the line goes up.

say.text: Last check. Equations tell stories. Here the number added is the starting value.

ask.q: A plant's height in cm after x weeks is y = 2x + 6. What does the 6 mean?
ask.right: The height at the start, when x = 0.
wrong: How much it grows each week.
ask.why: b is the starting value, which is the output when x = 0. Here that is 6 cm. The 2 is the growth each week, because it is the slope.

say.text: One warning. This form works for lines that are not vertical. A vertical line has no slope, so it can't be written as y = mx + b.
To finish, here is today in four lines. Next class we solve linear equations in one variable. Well done today.

show.text:
y = mx: a line through the origin
y = mx + b: b is where it crosses the y-axis, the starting value
Graph it: plot (0, b), then use rise over run
Write it: read b, find m, check with a point

notes.topic: Unit rate is the slope of y = mx
Linear functions with an initial value
Why slope is the same everywhere (similar triangles)

other_side.claim: Slope-intercept form, y = mx + b, is the easiest way to graph a line.
other_side.other_view: It is easiest when y is already by itself. OpenStax suggests a different method when the equation looks like Ax + By = C: find the two intercepts and join them. So the best form depends on how the equation is given.
